title: window, globalThis, process, and environment globals
hook: ECMAScript defines globalThis as the universal global reference — but browsers add window and DOM APIs while Node adds process, Buffer, and module. Isomorphic code must branch or polyfill carefully.

blocks.text: **globalThis**: standardized global object in any realm (browser, Node, Worker). **window**: browser global with DOM APIs. **global**: legacy Node alias. **process**: Node process info — `env`, `argv`, `exit`, signal handlers. **import.meta**: ESM metadata (`url`, `env` in Vite). **fetch** exists in both modern Node and browsers.

Libraries checking `typeof window !== "undefined"` to pick implementation — wrong check breaks in SSR. Leaking `process.env` secrets into client bundle when bundler inlines env vars. Workers use `self` not `window`.

blocks.title: Vite import.meta.env
blocks.body: Only VITE_ prefixed vars exposed to client — never DATABASE_URL in browser bundle.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Assuming window in Node SSR. Exposing all env to client bundle. Using global instead of globalThis in Workers.

blocks.text: Deno has Deno.env; Bun has Bun.env. Test isomorphic utils in vitest node and jsdom. Angular platform-browser vs platform-server split.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Uses window in Node. Puts secrets in VITE_ vars. Cannot name process SIGTERM handler.

interviewTakeaways: globalThis works everywhere; window is browser-only.
process.env Node; import.meta.env bundler client subset.
SSR: no window — branch storage and DOM.
60s: globalThis universal. window DOM browser. process Node env signals. Workers self. Never leak server env to client bundle.
Follow-up: graceful shutdown Node vs browser tab close?
commonPitfalls: Weak: localStorage in SSR without guard.
Strong: globalThis + environment branch + VITE_ only client.
